strengths: The at_2835 forward-collision gap (my r1 blocking concern) is genuinely closed, not papered over. Read the live test `at_2835_corpus_regression_anchor_matches_naive_reference` (crates/axc-driver/src/lib.rs:910-995): `naive_strip_reference` is a single-occurrence `source.find("@strategy")` reproduction and `strip_strategy_annotation_block` (lib.rs:365) is also currently single-block. The r2 fix (§5 table row + AT-2971: branch the RESIDUAL clause on block count -- use `strip_all_strategy_annotation_blocks` for >1-block files, leave the `== naive_strip_reference` EQUALITY clause untouched for all files) is structurally correct against the actual code: the equality clause only ever compares two single-strip outputs (so a 2-block file's single-strip-vs-single-strip equality is unaffected), and only the residual-liveness clause needed the branch. This is the right, minimal fix, not a broadened assertion that would silently weaken the OLD-vs-NEW pin.

The load_source / enumerate_variants attribution correction is verified accurate by direct source read. `crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/enumerate_variants.rs:80-82` contains the literal string "source must declare exactly one @kernel function" on a `hir.kernels.into_iter().next()` that does NOT actually count kernels -- confirmed the sole liar. `crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/load_source.rs:119-122` does `hir.kernels.into_iter().next().ok_or_else(...)` returning a generic empty `DriverError::Compile` with no 'exactly one' text at all -- confirmed silent-first-pick, a distinct defect, exactly as r2's §5 table and changelog item 5 now state. The Coder will not go hunting for nonexistent text in load_source.rs.

The §3 grid_search.rs citation ambiguity (my r1 minor note) is now disambiguated in-line: 'crates/axc-optimize/src/grid_search.rs:200 (the autotuner -- NOT the same-named MCP tool file crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/grid_search.rs, whose line 200 is unrelated)'. Verified both files exist and the distinction is real.

The comment-scope asymmetry rationale (my r2 focus item) holds up under independent verification via three separate code paths, not just assertion: (1) `strip_strategy_annotation_block`'s own doc comment (lib.rs:350-353) confirms the lexer already skips `//` comments and emits no `Annotation` token for comment-embedded text -- comments are gone before HIR, so they cannot affect emitted SPIR-V or golden bytes; (2) traced the ONE source-hash-keyed surface in the codebase, `history_path_for_source`/`source_xxh3` (crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/grid_search.rs:90,381,384; crates/axc-driver/src/mcp/tools/optimization_history.rs:73-74) -- the hashed `source` is the caller-supplied ORIGINAL pre-substitution text (from `resolve_source`), never the post-substitution resolved string; substitution happens per-variant, transiently, downstream of the hash and is never re-hashed or persisted to disk; (3) traced M3.19 log-opt's `splice_optimization_log_entry` (log_opt.rs:260-272) -- it NEVER calls `substitute_strategy_holes` at all (it operates on the raw un-resolved .axc file directly, and is unconditionally fail-closed on >1 kernel per its own `Multikernel` guard, so it never even sees a resolved multi-kernel source). So neither the M2.4 history path nor the M3.19 splice path can observe a comment-substitution artifact -- the two flagged historical footguns genuinely can't be reopened by F1's comment behavior. The asymmetry with the STRIP path (which IS lexer-anchored) is correctly reasoned: strip removes a whole span that could contain the wrong decoy block if mismatched, substitute only ever changes bytes that are semantically inert once past the lexer.

F1's boundary predicate (byte after the matched name not in [A-Za-z0-9_]) is not just plausible-sounding -- it is byte-for-byte the same identifier-continuation predicate the real lexer uses. Verified crates/axc-lexer/src/lexer.rs:219,246,487: `self.peek().is_ascii_alphanumeric() || self.peek() == b'_'`, i.e. exactly [A-Za-z0-9_], ASCII-only, no Unicode identifiers to worry about. F1's scan is therefore provably aligned with the actual token grammar, not an approximation that could itself introduce a new boundary bug.

New AT range is internally consistent: grepped all AT-29xx references in the spec -- 28 distinct IDs, contiguous AT-2945..AT-2972 with no gaps or collisions, matching both the stated range and the +5-ATs-since-r1 changelog claim.

The three pessimistic-review WARNINGs (wrong-metadata hazard, unenforced module-wide winner contract, strip_all termination predicate) map 1:1 onto r2's AT-2969 (distinct-dims fixture), AT-2970 (F4 negative-fixture cross-compile), and the explicit 'while changed, not while-token-exists' termination rule (§4 F2, API doc comment lib.rs signature block) -- all three are addressed with the exact mechanism the pessimistic reviewer's warnings called for, verified against the pessimistic JSON verdict directly.

validation_against_existing: F1's single-scan boundary-safe substitution is the standard token-boundary-guard pattern used by every real macro-substitution/text-templating engine that must avoid prefix collisions (e.g. C preprocessor macro-expansion's requirement that a replaced identifier not be a prefix of a longer identifier at the same site) -- this is not a novel or risky mechanism, it is the well-known fix for exactly this footgun class, and the spec's own framing ('third instance of an un-boundaried text transform') is accurate self-diagnosis, verified true against the two cited precedents (M3.14 comment-decoy find, M3.15 EB.3 strip) which are real, merged fixes in this codebase.

N-separate-modules-per-multi-stage-algorithm remains the correct Vulkan idiom (re-affirmed from r1): SPIR-V spec permits multiple OpEntryPoint per module (registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html §2.4/§3.32.2), but every published multi-pass GPGPU compute sample (Sascha Willems' Vulkan compute examples, NVIDIA's Vulkan compute patterns) uses separate pipelines per pass rather than a single multi-entry module -- the r2 hardening does not touch this core decision, correctly.

summary: Both items I flagged NEEDS_DISCUSSION on in r1 are genuinely closed, verified against the live source rather than taken on the Architect's word: the at_2835 forward-collision is fixed with a minimal, structurally-correct block-count branch (AT-2971) that leaves the load-bearing naive-reference equality untouched; the load_source/enumerate_variants attribution now matches what the two files actually contain. The pessimistic reviewer's CRITICAL (prefix-collision miscompile) and three WARNINGs are also verified closed by direct source inspection -- F1's boundary predicate is provably identical to the real lexer's identifier-continuation grammar (not an approximation), the wrong-metadata and winner-cross-validation hazards get dedicated proving ATs (2969, 2970) with fixtures specifically designed to catch what the shipped example (shared ?WG) would mask, and the strip_all termination predicate is correctly keyed on 'source changed' rather than 'token exists'. My assigned deep-dive question -- whether a substituted comment could reach a source-hash-keyed surface (M2.4 history path, M3.19 log-opt splice) -- checks out as sound on independent trace: the history hash is computed over the pre-substitution source (substitution happens per-variant, transiently, never re-hashed), and log-opt's splice never calls substitute_strategy_holes at all (it's unconditionally fail-closed on multi-kernel and operates on the raw unresolved file). The comment-vs-strip asymmetry is real and correctly reasoned, not a hand-wave. AT range (2945-2972, 28 distinct, contiguous, collision-free) and LOC budget (~1790/2200) are consistent with the stated deltas. No new inconsistency was found among the 5 new ATs. APPROVE.
